title: fel- and le-: felkel and lefekszik, Taken Apart

sections.title: The prefix hiding inside a word you already use every day
sections.content: Back in A1 you learned felkelek ('I get up') and lefekszem ('I go to bed') as fixed daily-routine phrases. Now look closer: fel- ('up') is glued onto kel ('rise'), and le- ('down') is glued onto fekszik ('lie'). Once you can see the seam, you can conjugate either half for any person, not just 'I'.

items.english: We go to bed at ten o'clock.

sections.content: fekszik is an -ik verb, just like eszik and iszik — its 'I' form is fekszem, not fekszek, and its plural forms run eszünk-style: fekszünk, feksztek, feksznek, not the regular -unk/-tok/-nak you'd expect from kel.
